highlights.title: Oracle tries to appease Stargate data center opponents with renewables push
highlights.summary: Oracle’s proposed investment in 2 gigawatts of renewable energy projects for New Mexico comes as local opposition could delay development of the Project Jupiter data center that Oracle is building for OpenAI.
body: The two tech companies are developing the $165 billion Project Jupiter data center in Santa Teresa, New Mexico, as part of the broader Stargate AI infrastructure project announced by President Donald Trump in 2025. But Project Jupiter faces local protests and court battles over concerns about its environmental impacts—and the latest Oracle announcement on September 8 seeking proposals for renewable energy projects does not change the fact that the data center will be powered by fuel cells that consume natural gas.

“Like all matching programs, this would be synthetic in the sense that 2 GW of renewables wouldn’t directly power the data center,” wrote Michael Thomas, CEO of the Cleanview data platform that tracks renewable energy and data center projects, in a LinkedIn post.

Oracle and OpenAI had originally planned to build 2.2 gigawatts of natural gas generation that could have resulted in 14 million tons of CO 2 emissions per year, Thomas pointed out. That would have effectively “wiped out 20 years of carbon emissions reductions in the state of New Mexico,” he wrote in his post.

highlights.title: Anthropic spent this week in hot water over cybersecurity
highlights.summary: After admitting earlier this year that its AI models had hacked other companies' systems on a handful of occasions, Anthropic released a new report on Wednesday detailing the attacks.
body: A researcher’s resignation letter went viral, just before the company released details about four models going rogue.

Anthropic’s incidents, though still concerning, were less coordinated and pervasive than the OpenAI incident that kicked off an industry-wide cybersecurity crisis this summer. That said, there are significant similarities. Anthropic said the most prevalent issues it discovered included a “willingness to take harmful actions in the narrow pursuit of a task,” similar to the “reward-hacking” that preceded the Hugging Face attack. Much like OpenAI, it said its prerelease tests and evaluations failed to catch severe risks.

Anthropic said it had signed an agreement with METR, one of the AI industry’s most prominent third-party AI evaluators, starting with an eight-week research agreement. The agreement grants METR access to transcripts “beyond the window in which the incidents occurred” (likely a subtle dig at OpenAI, which was criticized for limiting access in a deal with METR following the Hugging Face attack). It also said that METR would be able to chat directly with Anthropic employees, “who will be permitted to share confidential information.”

highlights.title: Remarkable Razaullah knock denies England series sweep inside three days
highlights.summary: England were denied a series sweep of Pakistan inside three days of the final Test at Edgbaston after a remarkable display of six-hitting from 21-year-old Razaullah late on Friday.
body: Pakistan enjoyed easily their finest day of what's otherwise been a dismal series but were still trailing by two when their eighth wicket fell early into the evening session, only for Razaullah to smash 81 off just 63 deliveries, clearing the ropes a staggering nine times to equal Tim Southee's record for a debutant.

He shared in a 121-run partnership with Mohammad Abbas (42), who himself hit two sixes before picking out point off Josh Tongue in the closing overs, while Razaullah's fun was finally ended - and the day's play - as he was stumped off Dan Lawrence (2-17).

England, guilty of losing the plot in the final session, will now look to chase down 130 on day four, a far stiffer target than initially looked likely, albeit one they should still reel in to clinch a first ever home series whitewash of Pakistan.
The tourists might be cursing not testing England further, with Shan Masood (95) and Babar Azam (76) both spurning golden opportunities to score the first century of the series.

highlights.title: Magic: The Gathering’s Newest Legendary Artifact Destroys Whole Universes (and Your Creatures)
highlights.summary: Magic: The Gathering’s next set is the world-bending Reality Fracture, which centers around an alternate universe with twisted mirror versions of many the game’s characters.
body: The first card is a key object in Reality Fracture: The Echoverse Fulcrum. This Mythic Rare legendary artifact is meant to merge universes together, but its functional effect is a board wipe with a little bit of card selection attached.

Colorless cards have had plenty of conditional board wipes like this before, but to my eyes, the low initial mana cost and immediate benefit of drawing and then discarding a card could make this one more broadly useful in a format like Commander. Five mana to activate its ability and only at sorcery speed are both real drawbacks, but that’s easier to stomach when you’ve already gotten something (admittedly minor) out of it.

The other card we are revealing depicts the final moments of Reality Fracture’s hero-turned-villain, Jace. Vraska’s Final Mercy is a Rare sorcery that can either be a removal spell or effectively draw you two cards as it either strikes down or builds up Jace himself.

highlights.title: One of AI’s Fiercest Critics Says All the Doom Talk Is ‘Meant to Distract Us’
highlights.summary: Timnit Gebru argues that AI companies are stoking fears of extinction to avoid discussing actual harms, like autonomous weapons.
body: The internet erupted into a debate about whether these fears are very legitimate, totally overblown, part of a regulatory capture strategy, or self-aggrandizement on the part of the AI labs that make the tech. Or some combination thereof.

Gebru has many thoughts on the AI-related events of this past week. While her work is essentially rooted in AI safety, she rejects phrases like “safety and alignment” and thinks those who are warning of our impending doom are trying to distract from the actual harms the tech industry might perpetuate.
LAUREN GOODE: What do you think all the attention on the “math fight” says about the current state of AI?

TIMNIT GEBRU: Well, first I would ask, why are they heavily investing in solving math problems? Why are they choosing certain disciplines? Somehow these subjects, like programming and chess and math, were elevated to mean, OK, you solved this and thereby you’ve solved intelligence. It’s so they can say, “We solved it.”

body: The New Mexico supreme court on Wednesday fined the attorney, Stephen Aarons, and held him in contempt for failing to verify the accuracy of the court ⁠filing, which Aarons said he prepared with help from the artificial intelligence ( AI ) application.
The filing “contained false testimony from wholly fabricated witnesses”, the court said.

The panel also said Aarons had “demonstrated a lack of remorse and a lack of concern ⁠for his client”. The justices fined Aarons $5,000 and said they will refer him to an attorney disciplinary board for investigation.

body: After being outpaced by his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the day's first session, Antonelli produced a quicker time of 1:33.662 in Practice Two to edge out Ferrari duo Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton by little more than a tenth of a second.

The timesheet was further evidence of Antonelli's sky-high confidence, which was elevated by a stunning victory at the Italian Grand Prix last weekend as he won his home race from 19th on the grid to move 66 points clear of Russell at the top of the standings with 10 rounds of the 2026 season remaining.

On the evidence of Friday's sessions, Mercedes and Ferrari are closely matched and could deliver an exciting pole contest in qualifying on Saturday, with huge excitement in the Spanish capital as F1 returns to the city for the first time since 1981.
Many had predicted a high number of red flags on Friday - and throughout the rest of the weekend - due to the tight and punishing nature of a circuit that the field have never raced at before.

highlights.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director says Square Enix would have to compromise "the quality of the final chapter" to ship the game fully on disc
highlights.summary: Physical versions of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation require a download anyway because Square Enix would've had to compromise the game in some fashion to contain the entire mammoth adventure in a disc. At least, that's the reasoning series director Naoki Hamaguchi has given.
body: Anyone sitting in the venn diagram middle of Final Fantasy 7 fan and physical games collector might have gone from extremely happy to kinda bummed earlier this week. The third and final part of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy is shipping in a physical format on all three major consoles (hurray), but you'll still need to download additional game data to get going.

"Each platform has limitations when it comes to physical media capacity, but we believed that compromising the quality of the final chapter in order to achieve a fully on-disc release would ultimately not be in the best interest of many fans," said Remake trilogy director Naoki Hamaguchi in an online statement.

"We understand that this decision may not meet everyone's expectations. Even so, in today's market, where the industry is steadily moving toward a disc-less future, we believe there is real value in being able to offer a physical edition at all," he added.

The collaboration sees players join Cody Rhodes on the hunt for John Cena’s in-game village, unlocking exclusive rewards as they seek out his base this month. The more players raid, the higher the chance of locating the elusive locale. There’s even a Cody Rhodes statue to be found.

highlights.title: ‘Like ‘Amores Perros,’ I Hope My Film Will Also Transcend Time in Some Way,’ Says Gael García Bernal of His Third Directorial Outing, ‘Hombre al Agua’
highlights.summary: Gael García Bernal is best known for his breakout roles in two of Mexico’s most consequential films, “Amores Perros” (2000) and “Y Tu Mama Tambien” (2001) but he’s also been directing these past years.
body: In “Hombre al agua,” García Bernal plays Camilo, a Cuban lifeguard who saves Abel, a Mexican businessman, from drowning. Grateful, Abel brings him to Mexico to work as his right-hand man and introduces him to his daughter, Juana, whom Camilo later marries. But he gradually realizes that his new life is part of a carefully orchestrated plan. As questions emerge about Abel’s motives, Camilo begins to piece together what is really happening and decides to take control of his future.
As the title suggests, roughly translated to “man overboard,” Camilo is adrift as his marriage falls apart and he tries to move beyond the lie he’s been living.

“I also wanted to explore the crisis of masculinity, the roles of men and women within a couple, and the experience of separation. I wanted to do all of this through comedy, with a kind of meta-cinematic playfulness, while also looking at the political landscape in Latin America today: where we are, what is happening and where we are going,” he said.
Reflecting on the impact of “Amores Perros,” he mused: “When it came out, it became something extraordinary and transcended time. Twenty-five years later, we’re still celebrating it.”

highlights.title: Matt Mullenweg reportedly returns as Automattic CEO two days after getting booted
highlights.summary: Two days after being placed on a paid leave of absence, Matt Mullenweg says he has been reinstated as CEO of Automattic, according to a Slack message seen by TechCrunch.
body: Automattic founder Mullenweg is apparently already back at the helm of Automattic — and is posting about ‘coup’ attempts.

As 404 Media reported on Wednesday, Mullenweg had told staff in Slack that CFO Mark Davies “conspired” with the board of directors, who voted to “put me on a paid leave of absence.” (Mullenweg said he voted against that.) He also told staff that the board had voted for Davies to become interim CEO. Davies, in a separate message, said that Mullenweg would still be a board member, according to 404 Media. An Automattic spokesperson told The Verge that Mullenweg was “currently on leave” from the company and confirmed Davies’ interim appointment.

In the message viewed by TechCrunch, however, Mullenweg wrote that the board is “back in agreement” and that he’s “in control of Automattic.” He added that “A lot happened in the past 48 hours that we need to sort out, and I hope much of it was a misunderstanding, because I have huge respect and regard for those involved.” TechCrunch reports that Davies’ Slack account has been deactivated and that Mullenweg had removed “all” admins from Automattic’s Slack.

He saddles four runners on the 250th anniversary of the great race including probable favourite Christmas Day, who is bidding to become the first Derby winner to triumph since Reference Point 39 years ago.

Aidan's son Joseph O'Brien looks the most likely opponent to spoil the Ballydoyle party with the impressive Enceladus, who steps up to Group One company for the first time after excelling in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Group Three Gordon Stakes at Goodwood.

However, I believe Aidan can complete the feat - not with Christmas Day but with his tough stable companion PIERRE BONNARD, who finished in front of him in the Great Voltigeur Stakes at York last month. This more demanding test of stamina is what he's been crying out for, and he can write his own piece of history.

highlights.title: Meta says it’s changing AI suggestions after posing invasive personal questions
highlights.summary: Meta says it's making changes to the prompts suggested by its AI chatbot after a viral video showed it digging for personal information about a woman's young daughters, as reported earlier by Futurism.
body: The change comes after a viral video showed Meta AI prompting a user to identify the child in one of her videos.

Last week, Instagram user Kalie Robins posted a video explaining how Meta AI presented her with an invasive suggestion after cross-posting a clip to Facebook. The AI prompt, “Who is the child passenger?” appeared beneath a video of her and her child singing in the car. When she selected the prompt, Robins says Meta AI pieced together information about her daughters from her previous posts, as well as posts from her relatives. It suggested additional prompts asking about her children’s ages and where Robins lives with her family. Robins says Meta AI also showed photos of her daughters posted to the platform, including one she claims she deleted years ago.

Meta has built its AI assistant into Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger, where it can answer questions, write posts, and generate images. In July, the company pulled a feature that allowed people to create AI deepfakes of other Instagram users after facing fierce backlash. Meta’s El-Kassaby now says it has fixed the issue causing Meta AI to suggest prompts related to personal topics.

highlights.title: Metroid Ravenous’ Surprise Reveal Was Secretly the Star of Nintendo’s Busy Week
highlights.summary: It was quite the week for Nintendo. A pair of back-to-back Direct showcases gave fans a lot to talk about, even if not all the news was equally exciting. The headliner of the week, of course, was The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
body: But that’s not the game occupying space in my brain following Nintendo’s busy week. That honor belongs to Metroid Ravenous. Samus’ new 2D adventure, which is set to lead the 2027 charge on Jan. 28, is looking like the Switch 2’s most stylish, exciting exclusive to date — at least based on a strong debut trailer that features Samus eating her enemies. We’ll only have to wait a few short months to find out if it lives up to its predecessor, the Game of the Year-nominated Metroid Dread, but it’s a good reminder that Nintendo’s current remake craze is paying off in the long-run.

The road to Metroid Ravenous started with a remake. Nintendo shocked Metroid fans back at E3 2017 when it revealed that it was remaking Metroid 2: Return of Samus as Metroid: Samus Returns, a full reimagining for the Nintendo 3DS. Even more surprising was that development on it was being led by MercurySteam. It sounded like a left-field choice, given that the team had no real connection to Nintendo, but it made perfect sense given that the studio was behind 2010’s well-received Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. Why not hand the keys to a small developer who already knew the Metroidvania genre?

highlights.title: August 2026 mobile game charts: Fate/Grand Order’s big anniversary, Valorant Mobile's rise and Brawl Stars’ worst month of the year
highlights.summary: Below you can see the latest top games and companies by downloads and revenue for August 2026, as well as the big stories and trends from the last month. Data is provided by AppMagic. Check out profiles of the world's top publishers in the Top 50 Mobile Game Makers 2025 list.
body: Note that these estimates are based on gross revenue from player spending across the App Store and Google Play only. It does not feature estimates from alternative marketplaces or direct-to-consumer platforms.

Aniplex’s long-running gacha Fate/Grand Order has seen player spending spike to its highest monthly sum of the year. The game made $57.7 million this August with an anniversary celebration in Japan, more than doubling July’s $22.5m.

In fact, this was the anime-style RPG’s best month since last August. The game makes 89% of its earnings from Japan, meaning the month is a major one each year - more than the North American anniversary in early July.

On a daily spending basis, earnings reached their highest in more than five years this August. Fate/Grand Order generated $4.6m on the 15th, surpassing any daily record from the past five anniversaries but not quite matching the game’s lifetime high of $5.6m on January 1st, 2021.

highlights.title: Self-driving cars should be taxed to offset job losses, thinktank urges
highlights.summary: Report says widespread autonomous vehicle adoption would put hundreds of thousands of private hire jobs at risk. Taxes on self-driving cars should be introduced now in the UK to offset the rise in congestion and threats to jobs they pose, a thinktank has urged.
body: The first robotaxis on London’s streets only started this month, but government projections are that up to 40% of cars sold could have self-driving capability by the middle of the next decade.

The report says widespread autonomous vehicle (AV) adoption would put hundreds of thousands of private hire jobs at risk, while individual ownership is likely to increase car usage at the expense of public transport, and increase congestion.

Introducing charges now on self-driving vehicles could ease the transition and provide a future revenue stream to replace dwindling fuel duty, according to the report from Centre for British Progress, a non-partisan thinktank focused on economic growth.
Wayve, a British tech firm pioneering autonomous cars, said it would “penalise the UK’s most promising innovators”.

highlights.title: Lifesaving Lincoln Laboratory device wins 2026 Excellence in Technology Transfer Award
highlights.summary: The handheld catheterization device AI-GUIDE, created by Lincoln Laboratory and Massachusetts General Hospital, promises improved health outcomes for injured service members and civilians.
body: The Federal Laboratory Consortium (FLC) selected AI-GUIDE, a medical device developed by MIT Lincoln Laboratory and Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH), for its 2026 Excellence in Technology Transfer Award. This award recognizes federal laboratories and collaborators who have accomplished outstanding work in the process of transferring technology. With funding from the U.S. Army's Combat Casualty Care Research Program (CCC), Lincoln Laboratory and MGH developed AI-GUIDE and are in the process of transferring the prototype to the startup company AutonomUS Medical Technologies, Inc.

"This recognition reflects what effective technology transfer looks like — aligning the Army's operational need with Mass General's clinical expertise and Lincoln Laboratory's engineering capabilities to deliver a solution with a clear path to impact. The transition to AutonomUS underscores how strong partnerships can carry a technology from development into real-world adoption," says Asha Rajagopal, Lincoln Laboratory's chief technology transfer officer.

body: “There are people that you don’t see from the outside, but I think he’s somebody that works extremely hard,” were Zverev’s words about Khachanov during his press conference yesterday.

He’s on the practice courts more than most people. He’s always searching for solutions. He’s always trying to find new ways to get better. He has a great coach who I’ve known also since juniors. He’s been with him since juniors. That I respect a lot when people go together for a long time and go together a long way.
We call him ‘The Professor’ because he knows everything about tennis, and he knows every single string tension, knows what everybody does, so that’s quite fun.

Zverev leads the career head-to-head 6-3 against Khachanov. They faced each other twice during the North American swing last year, with Khachanov winning in the Canadian Open semis but retiring in the fourth round at Cincinnati. Their only grand slam meeting was at the 2018 French Open, when Zverev won in five sets in the fourth round.

highlights.title: Stephanie Ahn’s Seven-Year Road to ‘Bedford Park’: ‘You Never Know What Can Make Your Film Better’
highlights.summary: After winning the U.S. Dramatic Special Jury Award for Debut Feature at Sundance this year, “Bedford Park” has its international premiere at the Toronto Film Festival, ahead of a U.S. theatrical release by Sony Pictures Classics.
body: This tension is embodied by Audrey, a physical therapist with a repressed fighting spirit and slightly kinky sexual encounters. When she meets Eli, a Korean American adoptee, in not-so-ideal circumstances, their relationship blossoms into a romance that redefines them. The story unfolds in the New Jersey suburbs, where Audrey goes back to live with her parents.

“I auditioned for Audrey seven years ago,” remembers Moon Choi. “It’s rare but Stephanie arranged to send me the whole script ahead of the audition. I read it in one sitting.” This project has been the longest the actress has ever waited to film, as COVID, Hollywood strikes and lack of funding kept threatening production. “I grew old with Audrey,” adds Choi. “I was 31 when I was cast and filmed at 37. It changed my understanding of many scenes.”

Throughout, the script remained the project’s fixed point. It changed considerably over the years, shifting from a family drama into a love story. “I didn’t want a traditional love story. I wanted to make the feeling of them getting together feel inevitable — but not predictable,” says Ahn.

The 21-year-old's audacious 81 from 63 balls frazzled England and propelled Pakistan to 449. His nine sixes tied Ben Stokes' record for the number of maximums in a Test innings in England.

Pakistan deserved to drag the match into a weekend, restoring a modicum of pride to what has been a shambolic tour.

highlights.title: How to fly helicopters in Wardogs
highlights.summary: If you want to level up your pilot skill, you need to know how to fly a helicopter in Wardogs. The latest hit FPS game has a skill system that is all about actually doing actions, such as spotting enemies, healing allies, and ferrying passengers to the battlefield.
body: If you want to be able to take allies to the battlefield without crashing directly into a tree or hitting the ground too quickly, here's a quick guide on how to fly in Wardogs.

Helicopters are the only aerial vehicle in Wardogs right now and while there are a few different types available, the MH-6 is the cheapest, easiest to fly, and by far the most recommended. There's no point investing in the Z20 Lakota or Havoc until you're a master at flying safely, and you don't want to worry about the AH-6 variants with weapons because your job is to be a pilot first and foremost. Also, the MH-6 is the only one you'll even be able to buy until you've earned more pilot experience.

When it comes to actually getting that little bird in the air, Kane Allard, a senior producer on Wardogs told me at Gamescom that he recommends pilots abandon mouse and keyboard entirely. Instead, switch to a controller whenever you're piloting a chopper, because it's much easier to control. After testing out this theory, he's bang on the money.

highlights.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users
highlights.summary: Learn how OpenAI evolved Habitat from a Python library into a globally distributed storage platform serving 1 billion ChatGPT users and 22M requests per second.
body: Every OpenAI product depends on fast, reliable access to data, whether someone is logging in, checking their Codex settings, or starting a new conversation in ChatGPT. Each of those actions may require many separate data lookups before the product can respond. If those requests are slow, the product feels slow. If those requests fail, the product stops working entirely.

Habitat is the online storage platform we built so OpenAI products can quickly and reliably access needed information. Habitat now handles more than 70 million requests every second, supporting products used by over 1 billion people each week, across almost 40 geographic regions. Two years ago, Habitat started as a simple Python client-side library connected to a single database. Today, it’s a complex distributed system that serves more than 500 petabytes of data.

body: "Guarding the secrets of the unique gameplay and design are akin to Apple protecting the iPhone or Coke protecting its formula," Rockstar said in its opening note (via IGN ). The company claims that people are so hell-bent on peeking behind the curtain that it was forced to coat its building windows with a privacy film after aerial drones were used to spy on employees and photograph the inside of the building. highlights.title: Living with tinnitus can be distressing. So what can you do about it?
highlights.summary: Tinnitus affects millions of people and it can take many different forms. But there are therapies that can help make it more bearable. For some it’s a high-pitched mosquito whine; for others it’s a low bass hum.
body: Whatever form it takes, tinnitus – hearing sounds like ringing, buzzing or hissing when no external noise is there – can be extremely distressing because it’s quite literally in your head; there is no escaping it. Given that at least one-quarter of the population report experiencing tinnitus at some stage in their life, it’s surprising how little is understood about why.

“The theory that’s most supported at the moment is that there’s some sort of change in the hearing pathway, and the nerves in the hearing pathway are basically firing more than they should do,” says Dr Emma Laird, an audiologist at La Trobe University in Melbourne. “We’re hearing this increased activity as that tinnitus sound.”

There is no cure for tinnitus but the good news is that there is a variety of treatment approaches – audiological, psychological, physiotherapeutic and technological – that can be effective at helping people to manage the condition. “I’ve had tinnitus for probably 20 years now,” Laird says. “Because I’ve habituated to it – so my brain can just pop it at the back of my head – it’s not causing distress day to day.”
points: Tinnitus affects millions of people and it can take many different forms.
But there are therapies that can help make it more bearable.

“I’ve had tinnitus for probably 20 years now,” Laird says.
